rules.C1: evidence without more-steps/OOD extrapolation caps at 5; +1 for a grounded intermediate target (per-pass NCP code or sg(final plan))
rules.status: C1/C2 are evidence-based projections, not results; the per-pass eval sheet (E1–E15) decides. D3's lead rests on puzzle/pixel-regime evidence (Diffusion-Timestep, URM, TRM/GRAM) — read 70.5 as a bet.

chassis: Position in the model: the middle-span core between the encoder and the decoder; interface unchanged: `forward(c_hat, cdoc, R) -> u, logits, c_pred` (D3/D5 also return per-pass logits for the per-pass loss).

Width: in-projection W_in 384 → 256 on c_hat (X̃), separate start projection W_s 384 → 256 (S_0 = W_s c_hat ≠ 0, so the two read branches differ from step 0), out-projection W_out 256 → 384 for the decoder plan (small non-zero init).

Block: FOUR DISTINCT layers, d 256, SwiGLU FFN 1024, FULL causal attention over all 256 chunk positions (doc-masked; not windowed), 4 heads × 64 with GQA kv 2, sigmoid output gate, NoPE; the q/k/v shortconvs of today's layer are removed (URM). One pass = one cycle through the 4 layers.
S-space: every sublayer reads [X̃, S] through the Qwen-GR elementwise gated read (low-rank 32) and writes the carry S.
Identity at init: exactly one zero-init per path (the block output projections W_o / W_2), except where stated.
PQ: stays 48 segments × 128 codes × 8 dims in c_hat space (336 bits/chunk); NCP head W_q 256 → 384 + distance head.
No pass-index conditioning (default-off for extrapolation designs), except D2 (LoopFormer's normalised (t, Δ)).
Budget denominators: non-core MACs 26.765M/token; row 0 core 1.99M/token at eval R 4 (6.9 %); cap 25 %.

ROW0.title: Today: ConceptCoreV2

why.C1: GRT-style recipe (random r, loss at sampled depth) is the one paper result that converges to a fixed point
why.C2: measured: R1..R8 equal, step angle 6.7 -> 0.1 deg
why.C4: u carries about one answer token
why.C6: not identity at init, carry grows +8.5 per pass

ROW0.heading: Row 0 — today's ConceptCoreV2
spec: One shared d-384 LoopLayer, R ~ U{1..4}, S_0 = 0, not identity at init, unbounded carry, loss at the sampled R. 2.06M params · 1.99M MACs/token at R 4 (6.9 %). Measured: R1..R8 equal, step angle 6.7° → 0.1°, OOD more-steps 0.

D1.title: S-FIX

why.C1: Loop-Think extrapolates with large Poisson R + zero-init, but on a parametric toy task; no grounded per-pass target
why.C2: pre-committed 4-5: placement unchanged, sampled-R loss can still be minimised by invariance on easy chunks
why.C3: 4 distinct d-256 layers cycled up to 8x
why.C5: single trajectory, decoder sees final plan
why.C6: identity at init, clamped carry, full BPTT through 32 layers

D1.vs_row0: Removes baseline defects 1 (not identity at init), 2 (train R max 4) and 4 (growing carry) and adds 4 distinct layers; keeps the loss placement, so it tests whether init + R alone caused R1..R8 = equal. Confirmed if E5 step angle stays > 1° past pass 4 and E4 agreement between passes 4 and 8 is < 1.
D1.heading: D1 — S-FIX (minimal fix of today's loop) · C2 mechanism (i) large random train R
spec: Carry: norm clamp S ← S / max(rms(S)/ρ, 1) after each pass. Write: today's GR write scalar.
R ~ clip(Poisson(4), 2, 8) per sequence (E[R] 4.08); eval R 4; sweep to 16; optional KL+entropy halting.
Loss: NTP + NCP at the final pass of the sampled R only (placement deliberately unchanged) + VQ.
Fixes audit 1 (init), 2 (R_max 8), 4 (clamp); keeps audit 3 by design. Expected C2 4–5/10 (GRT counter-evidence).
Budget: 4.91M params · 4.83M MACs/token at R 4 (15.3 %) · training ×1.13.

D2.title: LOOPFORMER-S

why.C1: LoopFormer 1B/25B: no stagnation (low cross-step CKA), elasticity; grounded via sg(u_L); not more-steps extrapolation
why.C2: main loss on R=L, shortcut distilled to the long endpoint: the exact asymmetry audit item 3 asks for
why.C5: decoder trained on long and (every 4th batch) short plans: usable at any R <= 6
why.C6: AdaLN warm-up risk at 25M (pre-committed penalty); two trajectories
why.C8: second trajectory + conditioning MLP; moderate trainer change

D2.vs_row0: Removes defect 3 exactly as LoopFormer does (main loss on the long route, short route distilled to it) plus defects 1, 2, 4; targets the measured stagnation directly ('concept drift'). Confirmed if E11 cross-pass CKA stays low and quality rises monotonically with R = 1..6 (E12).
D2.heading: D2 — LOOPFORMER-S (the user's favourite, faithfully) · C2 mechanism (iii) shortcut-consistency self-distillation
spec: AdaLN(t, Δ) per layer; α(c) is the write gate (GR write scalar dropped), α init 0.05, modulation (1 + γ(c)) after the GR read.
Init EXCEPTION: in D2 W_o / W_2 keep DEFAULT init — α is the single near-zero factor on the path.

Long trajectory L = 6 passes (4 × 6 = 24 effective layers = LoopFormer 3 ⊗ 8) + one shortcut S ~ U{1..5} (Dirichlet schedule, big-early); the shortcut path reads sg(X̃) and starts from sg(S_0) — W_in / W_s get gradient only from the long trajectory.
Loss: NTP(u_L) + NCP(u_L) + 0.1·NCP(u_S) + 0.1·‖sg(u_L) − u_S‖² + decoder on the shortcut plan every 4th batch (weight 0.1) + VQ.
Claim: budget elasticity (any R ≤ 6), NOT more-steps extrapolation. Eval R 6 (big-early or uniform schedule; E13 compares).
Budget: 6.08M params · 7.19M MACs/token at R 6 (21.2 %) · training ×1.41 (2 NCP head evaluations).

D3.title: DEEP-SUP GROUPS

why.C1: strongest evidence: Diffusion-Timestep K<=160 -> 10,000; URM; TRM/GRAM 16 -> 256; grounded per-pass NCP target; puzzles not LM
why.C2: detached windows force each window to improve the previous state; equal per-pass loss is the evidenced pairing
why.C4: PQ unchanged; multimodal target may settle-then-wander
why.C5: heavier NCP weighting (mean over passes); X-bypass risk
why.C6: LN_h carry, per-window backward bounds memory
why.C8: per-pass logits + per-window backward: trainer change

D3.vs_row0: Replaces the loss that rewards R-invariance with detached windows that must improve the previous state, each pass supervised by the true next-chunk code (grounded). Confirmed if E11 per-window NCP improvement is ≤ 0 on average and hop/bind rise at R = 8–16 (E2).
D3.heading: D3 — DEEP-SUP GROUPS · C2 mechanism (ii) detached-carry improvement operator
spec: Carry h = LN_h(S) with its own gain; separately normed readout (Diffusion-Timestep dual views).

K ~ U{8..12} passes (E[K] 10) so EVERY sample has ≥ 2 windows ([4,4], [4,5], [4,6], [4,7], [4,4,4]) — with K < 8 a sample would be one BPTT graph with equal per-pass loss, the unevidenced regime; windows of 4, remainder merged into the last window; BPTT inside a window, carry DETACHED between windows; ALL windows graded; per-window backward. Eval R 6 lies inside window 2 for every K.
Loss: MEAN per-pass NCP over all passes (grounded per-pass target) + NTP on the final pass + VQ.
Main risk: X̃ is clean every pass → windows may ignore the carry (E13 gate mass; X̃-dropout ablation). Multimodal target may settle-then-wander (E12).
Budget: 4.91M params · 7.19M MACs/token at R 6 (21.2 %) · training ×1.40.

D4.title: LOOPED-MoE + DELTA-RES

why.C1: Sparse-Layers (iso-FLOP LM): looped dense FFN is the bottleneck, MoE routing diverges across passes, 4x4 best; Delta-Res 220M-8B; no step extrapolation test
why.C2: as D1 (4) +1 for EBT's random per-pass step scale, the ingredient EBT found most important for gains that grow with steps
why.C3: state-conditioned per-pass experts + early-pass retrieval; CONDITIONAL: rises to 8 only if E11 shows routing divergence and E15 layer specialisation (shared pool untested — Sparse-Layers used per-layer pools)
why.C6: MoE at chunk rate: load balance noisy; shared pool untested

D4.vs_row0: Removes the 'same dense op every pass' invariance: state-conditioned experts make each pass compute differently, and a Delta Attention Residual lets pass r retrieve early passes instead of an overwritten S. Confirmed if E11 routing divergence across passes and E15 per-layer specialisation appear, with Delta-Res routing sharp (E14).
D4.heading: D4 — LOOPED-MoE + DELTA-RES · C2 mechanism (i) as D1; novelty = state-conditioned per-pass computation (C3)
spec: FFN → one expert pool shared by the 4 layers: 8 SwiGLU experts × 512, top-2 (active width 1024), per-layer routers, LB + z-loss (16 experts = ablation).
Delta Attention Residual over per-pass deltas: 6 slots {X̃, null (value 0, live), last 4 pass-deltas (masked −∞ when absent)}, zero-init queries (uniform routing), additive.
EBT random step scale ξ ~ U[0.5, 1.5] on each pass's writes in training (ξ = 1 at eval). Carry clamp as D1. R as D1.
Pre-committed: C2 4–5 (as D1); C3 only if routing diverges across passes (E11 per layer) and experts specialise per layer (E15).
Budget: 4.92M params · 4.86M MACs/token at R 4 (15.4 %) · training ×1.13.

D5.title: K-PLAN

why.C1: D3's evidence for the schedule; Explorative Modeling says AR LMs are its hardest case (modest gains) — scored weakest per pre-commitment (K-plan novelty has the weakest evidence)
why.C4: K=4 candidate plans cover several valid continuations; leak <= 2 bits/chunk
why.C5: selector error = train/infer mismatch; multimodal middle unbounded until E13 measures it
why.C6: soft-min prevents seed starvation; more moving parts
why.C7: 24.2 % at R 4 (at the cap), training x1.49

D5.vs_row0: Adds what a single deterministic plan cannot hold: K = 4 candidate plans for a next chunk with several valid continuations, leak-bounded (≤ 2 bits/chunk), on D3's detached schedule. Confirmed if E13 NTP with the selected plan beats one-plan D3 and the selector's top-1 (E11) is well above chance.
D5.heading: D5 — K-PLAN (leak-bounded multimodal plan) · C2 mechanism (ii) as D3; novelty = plan capacity (C4)
spec: D3 chassis (LN_h carry) with K ~ U{8..10} (E[K] 9; ≥ 2 detached windows per sample, narrowed vs D3 to stay ≤ 1.5× training) + LATE-BRANCH fork: passes 1..R−1 shared; the last pass runs for K = 4 learned seeds.
Soft-min training: weights softmax(−sg(CE_k)/τ), τ 1.0 → 0.3 (no seed starvation); leak ≤ 2 bits/chunk, ≤ 4 bits visible to a decoder position.

Selector: value head (256 → 64 → 1) trained by KL to the same soft target; inference uses its pick; 25 % of batches feed the decoder sg(selected plan) (robustness to selector error, no gradient into the core).
C1 weakest (Explorative Modeling: autoregressive LMs are its hardest case). R 4 design (R 6 exceeds the cap).
Budget: 4.93M params · 8.53M MACs/token at R 4 (24.2 %) · training ×1.48.

D6.title: LOOPFORMER-MoE-DS

why.C1: inherits D3's evidence (Diffusion-Timestep 160 -> 10,000, URM, TRM/GRAM; grounded per-pass NCP) with the same puzzle-regime discount; Sparse-Layers (LM, iso-FLOP) for looped MoE
why.C2: D3's detached windows + LoopFormer consistency in the final window; the extra point over D3 rests on an ARGUMENT (state-routed experts give the carry a job X̃ cannot do), not evidence — capped at 9
why.C3: 4 distinct layers x 8-12 passes with state-conditioned experts; conditional +1 (to 8) only if E11/E15/E16 show routing divergence and layer specialisation
why.C5: heavier NCP weighting as D3; decoder sees only the final plan
why.C6: most moving parts of any design except D5: windows + MoE + per-window LB + consistency
why.C8: per-pass logits + per-window backward + MoE router/LB: largest trainer change after D5

D6.vs_row0: Attacks all three causes of today's 'passes don't matter': the loss (LoopFormer's distillation toward the endpoint in the final window), the optimisation signal (D3's detached windows, every pass graded on the true next-chunk code) and the computation (D4's experts routed on the state, so each pass computes differently). Confirmed if E16 shows window 2 routing differently from window 1, E17 shows drift in the final window, and hop/bind rise at R = 8–16.
D6.vs_others: vs D3: experts routed on the state give the carry a job, so windows cannot just recompute from X̃ (D3's E13 risk). vs D4: D3's detached windows replace D4's sampled-R loss, which can be satisfied by invariance. vs D2: keeps LoopFormer's consistency where it is well-defined and gets per-pass variation from routing that exists at any R, so it is not limited to elasticity within the trained depth.
D6.heading: D6 — LOOPFORMER-MoE-DS (best of D2 + D3 + D4, user request) · C2 mechanism (ii) + LoopFormer consistency + state-routed experts
spec: Scope stated honestly: D3's training (detached windows, every pass graded on the true next-chunk code) + LoopFormer's consistency ‖sg(u_K) − u_r‖² (weight 0.1) applied only to the passes of the FINAL window + D4's experts in every layer and pass.

Where LoopFormer lives: its training recipe (distil late passes toward the endpoint); its (t, Δ) conditioning is replaced by experts routed on the state (ablation A1 keeps it testable, with D2's wiring).

FFN: one shared pool of 8 SwiGLU experts × 512, top-2 (active width 1024), per-layer routers; load-balance + z-loss accumulated per window and backpropagated with that window; fallback per-layer E = 8 if the pool collapses (E15).
Chassis as D3: S_0 = W_s c_hat, LN_h carry, K ~ U{8..12}, windows of 4 (remainder merged), per-window backward; eval R 6.
Decisive checks: E16 routing divergence across windows (does the carry get a job), E17 drift in the final window, A4 dense FFN (does looped MoE matter at this scale), A2 consistency off.
Budget: 4.92M params · 7.20M MACs/token at R 6 (21.2 %) · training ×1.40.
